title: Route-based VPN with a VTI
blurb: Replace the crypto map with an IPsec virtual tunnel interface and route traffic into it.
scenario: The crypto map from Lab 5 works, but every new subnet means editing the crypto ACL on both sides. Convert R1 to a **static virtual tunnel interface (VTI)**: traffic is encrypted because it's **routed** into **Tunnel0**. Reuse the IKEv2 profile **PROF-R2** and the transform set **TS** you built before.
objectives: Route the remote LAN into the tunnel

steps.title: Policy-based or route-based?
steps.learn: A **crypto map** is policy-based: an ACL decides what's encrypted. A **VTI** is route-based: anything routed into the tunnel is encrypted, and the tunnel is a real interface, so it can run routing protocols, QoS and per-interface features.
steps.task: Pick the advantages of a VTI over a crypto map.
steps.question: Which statements are true of a VTI?

options.text: Dynamic routing protocols such as OSPF or EIGRP can run over the tunnel.
New subnets only need a route, not crypto ACL changes on both peers.

options.why: A VTI still uses IKE (here IKEv2) to negotiate keys.

options.text: It encrypts with GRE instead of ESP.
options.why: `tunnel mode ipsec ipv4` uses ESP directly, with no GRE header.

steps.title: IPsec profile
steps.learn: An **IPsec profile** plays the crypto map's role for tunnel interfaces. It names the transform set and the IKEv2 profile, and it has no peer or ACL, because the tunnel destination and routing provide those.
steps.task: Create IPsec profile **VTI-PROF** using transform set **TS** and IKEv2 profile **PROF-R2**.
steps.hint: `crypto ipsec profile VTI-PROF`, `set transform-set TS`, `set ikev2-profile PROF-R2`.

steps.title: Tunnel interface
steps.task: Create **Tunnel0** with address **172.31.0.1/30**, source **GigabitEthernet0/0**, destination **198.51.100.2**, mode **ipsec ipv4**, and protection profile **VTI-PROF**.
steps.hint: `interface Tunnel0`, `ip address 172.31.0.1 255.255.255.252`, `tunnel source GigabitEthernet0/0`, `tunnel destination 198.51.100.2`, `tunnel mode ipsec ipv4`, `tunnel protection ipsec profile VTI-PROF`.

commands.output: %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface Tunnel0, changed state to up
commands.note: The tunnel came up as soon as IKEv2 finished with R2.

steps.title: Route into the tunnel
steps.task: Remove the old crypto map from **GigabitEthernet0/0**, and add a static route to **10.2.2.0/24** through **Tunnel0**.
steps.hint: `interface GigabitEthernet0/0`, `no crypto map CMAP`, then `ip route 10.2.2.0 255.255.255.0 Tunnel0`.

commands.note: Anything routed to the branch is now encrypted by the tunnel.

commands.output:
Tunnel0 is up, line protocol is up
  Hardware is Tunnel
  Internet address is 172.31.0.1/30
  Tunnel source 203.0.113.1 (GigabitEthernet0/0), destination 198.51.100.2

summary: An IPsec profile reusing the IKEv2 profile and transform set, a static VTI in IPsec mode, the crypto map removed, and a static route sending the branch LAN into the tunnel.
